name: Cable straight-through joint
summary: A joint connecting two lengths of the same cable in line, drawn as a mark on the cable route.
description: The straight-through joint connects two cable lengths end to end, restoring insulation, screen and sheath continuity. It is shown on cable route drawings and network diagrams at joint bay positions, because joints are the most common failure points on long underground circuits and their locations are needed for fault finding.

The symbol does not show whether screens are cross-bonded at the joint, which is common on high voltage single-core circuits. Cross-bonding links and sheath voltage limiters are separate items on the bonding diagram. It also does not distinguish a joint made between identical cables from one between different types, which is a transition joint.
readingNotes: Note joint locations for fault-location records.
Check for screen cross-bonding at the joint.
drawingChecklist: Show each joint at its route chainage.
distinction: A straight-through joint links two lengths of the same cable; a branch joint takes off a second cable.
